chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Faraj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked my brother while I was present: 'Regarding the garment that is dyed with safflower and then washed, do you wear it while you are in the state of Ihram?' He said: 'Yes, for safflower is not perfume, but I dislike that you wear what makes you conspicuous to people.'
And if something of the perfume of the Kaaba or its saffron touches the garment of the one in Ihram, that does not harm him, even if he does not wash it.

key_terms.الطِّيبِ: Perfume/fragrance (specifically the scented plants that invalidate Ihram if worn)
key_terms.الْعُصْفُرِ: Safflower, a plant used for yellow dye
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear clothes dyed with safflower while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the legal invalidation of Ihram and the social etiquette of modesty, noting that while safflower dye is not a fragrant perfume (*tayyib*) that breaks the state, it is disliked if it draws undue attention. The hadith further clarifies that contact with the Kaaba’s specific perfume or saffron does not nullify Ihram, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between intrinsic ritual impurities and external, non-intrusive scents. This ruling underscores the principle that Ihram is primarily compromised by intentional use of known perfumes, rather than incidental exposure to blessed substances.
